slides.title: I See What You Want: Decoding Hierarchical Operator Intent from Visual Teleoperation History
slides.highlight: This work introduces a vision-language model that infers both atomic actions and broader missions from visual teleoperation history, significantly outperforming proprietary LLMs. The resulting intent predictions enable autonomous policies to take over tasks mid-execution, reducing human teleoperation time by approximately 35%.

card.one_liner: VIM decodes hierarchical operator intent from visual teleoperation history to enable autonomous task continuation.
card.key_idea: Fine-tunes a VLM on VI AMO dataset to jointly predict ongoing atomic actions and missions from visual history and context.
card.evaluation: Tested on VI AMO (6,600 episodes) and real-world Franka arm tasks; outperforms GPT-4o/Luna in SBERT similarity and reduces teleoperation time by ~35%.
card.limitation: Lacks calibrated confidence estimates, relies on predefined action boundaries, and VLA execution speed may not match skilled operators.

slides.title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework where Vision-Language Models generate editable objective programs to guide Model-Predictive Controllers for contact-rich manipulation, bridging semantic reasoning with physics-based planning.

card.one_liner: VLMs generate editable multi-stage cost programs for contact-rich manipulation, refined via simulated MPC rollouts.
card.key_idea: Connects VLMs to sampling-based MPC via an objective program of staged costs from a library, iteratively refined using digital twin rollouts.
card.evaluation: Tested on four tabletop tasks in simulation (97.5% success) and real world (80%), outperforming VLA and MPC baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate digital twin physics; lacks explicit recovery mechanisms for failed stages and handles occlusion poorly.

slides.title: RUMI: A Robotiq-Matched Universal Manipulation Interface for Robot Learning with Augmented Reality and Haptic Feedback
slides.highlight: RUMI introduces a handheld manipulation interface matched to the Robotiq 2F-85 gripper, utilizing augmented reality and haptic feedback to facilitate the collection of large-scale, force-aware datasets for robot learning.

card.one_liner: RUMI is a Robotiq-matched handheld interface enabling force-aware data collection via augmented reality and haptic feedback.
card.key_idea: A scissor-linkage gripper matching Robotiq 2F-85 kinematics, featuring interchangeable tactile sensors, VR-based AR robot visualization, and a contact-triggered haptic blocker.
card.evaluation: User study showed fewer joint violations with AR; imitation policies trained on real/simulated tasks demonstrated higher success rates with tactile/haptic feedback.
card.limitation: Restricted to a single wrist-camera viewpoint and lacks external force feedback beyond the mechanical blocking mechanism.

slides.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile foundation model that unifies heterogeneous sensor data, enabling plug-and-play integration into embodied policies to enhance dexterous manipulation.

card.one_liner: LingBot-Touch creates unified tactile representations from heterogeneous sensors to enhance dexterous manipulation policies.
card.key_idea: Develops a tactile foundation model yielding unified, plug-and-play tokens across piezoresistive, magnetic, and visuotactile sensors.
card.evaluation: Validated via simulation and real-robot tests on multiple platforms, showing improved dexterity and efficiency in complex tasks.

slides.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: PCTac introduces an open-source mechanochromic photonic-crystal fingertip that encodes contact load directly into a spatially resolved hue field, bypassing indirect force inference. Integrated with Diffusion Policy, this structural-color representation achieved a 75.6% success rate across 90 physical rollouts, outperforming standard RGB tactile and vision-only baselines in dexterous manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: PCTac uses mechanochromic photonic crystals to encode contact force directly as hue changes for robot learning.
card.key_idea: A tactile fingertip converts local stress into structural color via photonic crystals, using reference-relative hue fields as direct policy observations.
card.evaluation: Tested on three real-robot tasks with Diffusion Policy; PCTac Hue achieved 75.6% success, outperforming RGB and vision-only baselines.
card.limitation: Limited sensitivity to concave features and ambiguity between normal and shear loads due to current elastomer properties.

slides.title: On the Utility of Pre-Trained Visual Representations for Policy Learning of Contact-Rich Insertion Tasks
slides.highlight: This study reveals that optimal visual representations for contact-rich manipulation are highly task-dependent, yet spatially-grounded, contact-centric information remains distinctively valuable for policy learning despite challenges in reliable estimation under visual noise.

card.one_liner: Visual representation benefits for contact-rich insertion are highly task-dependent and unpredictable.
card.key_idea: Compares vision foundation models against contact-centric features in insertion tasks, revealing sensitivity to occlusion and tolerance.
card.evaluation: Simulated peg/book insertion and real-world book insertion; measured success rates across data budgets and visual perturbations.
card.limitation: Results vary unpredictably with minor task changes; ground-truth contact features are impractical to estimate reliably in real-world noise.

slides.title: VOKE: Visual Object Kinematics Estimator for Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation
slides.highlight: VOKE enhances dexterous in-hand manipulation by estimating full object kinematics (velocity and acceleration) from visual data, improving pose accuracy and enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for reinforcement learning policies.

card.one_liner: VOKE augments pose estimators with explicit velocity and acceleration to improve dexterous in-hand manipulation.
card.key_idea: A pluggable module predicts kinematic states from temporal features, refining poses via second-order motion priors for policy learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on DexYCB/OakInk with three backbones; improves pose accuracy and reduces kinematic error vs. pose differencing; validated in sim-to-real.
card.limitation: Performance degrades under severe occlusion, extreme viewpoints, or rapid contact/slipping where acceleration estimation is difficult.

slides.title: DexRemo: A Force-Sensing Hand Platform and Task Suite for Contact-Rich Removal Manipulation
slides.highlight: Introduces a three-finger robotic hand with high-force actuation and three-axis fingertip force sensing, alongside a task suite for contact-rich removal manipulation. Demonstrates that expressing fingertip forces in a shared wrist-centered frame improves policy stability and generalization for tasks involving adhered or mechanically constrained targets.

card.one_liner: DexRemo introduces a force-sensing hand and task suite for contact-rich removal manipulation using wrist-frame force fusion.
card.key_idea: A three-finger hand with integrated force sensors transforms local fingertip forces into a shared wrist-centered frame for consistent multi-finger fusion in ACT-based imitation learning.
card.evaluation: Tested on nine real-robot tasks with 20 demonstrations each; ablations confirm wrist-frame forces improve stability and generalization over local-frame or no-force baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on only 20 demonstrations per task, potentially limiting robustness to complex contact dynamics not seen during training.
